# gitmoap_repository_catalog_services (Data Source)

List the services bound to a repository, each with its deployment promotion track. Returns every service with a path binding in this repository, alphabetically by slug, with the same filters and paging as the group listing. A service declared in a group you cannot see is left out, so a page can come back shorter than `limit` while still carrying a `next_token`.

The token needs `catalog:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_catalog_services" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) The repository the services are bound to

### Optional

- `include_orphaned` (Boolean) Include entries whose declaration has disappeared (excluded by default)
- `kind` (String) Filter by service kind
- `lifecycle_stage` (String) Filter by lifecycle
- `search` (String) Match the name, description or a slug substring
- `source` (String) Filter by how the entry came to exist

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `deployments` (Attributes List) At most one entry per tier, ordered `development`, `testing`, `staging`, `production`. Empty
for a `library`, an external service, or anything never deployed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--deployments))
- `service` (Attributes) The short form of a service that listings, search results and path lookups show. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--service))

<a id="nestedatt--items--deployments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.deployments`

Read-Only:

- `deployed` (Boolean)
- `status` (String) Where a deployment is in its life. It starts `requested`; waits as `awaiting_approval` when the
environment needs approval, ending `rejected` if refused; then `running`, ending `succeeded`,
`failed` or `cancelled`. `skipped` means another deploy held the environment and its policy is to
skip. A successful deployment becomes `superseded` when a later one replaces it.
- `tier` (String) What kind of environment this is, whatever it is called: `development`, `testing`, `staging`
or `production`. A `production` environment is protected by default.


<a id="nestedatt--items--service"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.service`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String)
- `external` (Boolean)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String) What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.
- `lifecycle` (String) Where a service is in its life.
- `orphaned_at` (String)
- `owner` (Attributes) Who owns a service: a group, a team, or a person or service account. A service may also have no
owner, which the `has_owner` scorecard check surfaces.

`kind` says which applies: `group`, with `full_path`, `group_id`; `principal`, with `actor`, `principal_id`; `team`, with `organization`, `slug`, `team_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--service--owner))
- `service_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)
- `source` (String) How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.

<a id="nestedatt--items--service--owner"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.service.owner`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--service--owner--actor))
- `full_path` (String)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String)
- `organization` (String) The full path of the organization's top-level group, such as `acme`.
- `principal_id` (String)
- `slug` (String) The team's slug, such as `backend`.
- `team_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--service--owner--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.service.owner.actor`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
